structure: Part 2 read in full: src/k6/journeys.js (the notification run every journey shares: INS sign-in, journey dashboard, create, draft chunks across sessions, re-edit, submit through the declaration, read back, amend then cancel or resubmit, backend replay of the first save), src/k6/returning-session.js (the endurance returning visit), src/k6/browser-session.js and its test (cookie jar, manual redirect following, sign-in hops, stub credential post, stale-save counting, page parsing of crumb, heading, hidden fields, form inputs and upload target), src/k6/pages.js (the walker: request-mix classification, think time, counters), src/lib/redirects.js and its test (path and origin reading, localhost aliasing, staleAction=1 detection, the /oauth2/authresp sign-in page, the sign-in hop paths /auth/, /oauth2/, /idphub/, /organisations, and reading the new id after /live-animals/notifications/), src/config/journey-endpoints.js (sharedEndpoints and journeyEndpoints only) and the live-animals entry of JOURNEYS in src/config/smoke.js. Pages covered: the live-animals set root '/live-animals' (animals-dashboard) and its '?referenceNumber=<id>' search (animals-dashboard-search), POST '/live-animals/notifications' (animals-create) landing on '/live-animals/notifications/<id>/origin', the hub '/live-animals/notifications/<id>' (animals-hub), notification-view, declaration and its save (declaration=confirmed) landing on '/confirmation', POST '<base>/amend' landing on notification-view, cancel-amend and its save landing on notification-view with cancelled=1, and resubmission through the declaration. The live-animals returning visit re-opens '/live-animals'. The question pages between create and review are part 3's; the plants half of the same files is out of scope. The page-path helper pagePath (src/k6/journey-pages.js:72, '<base>/<slug>') and the returning-animals entry (src/config/design-target.js:346) were looked up only to resolve paths these files use.

claims.statement: The live-animals journey's set root, the page a user starts from and returns to, is '/live-animals' on the animals frontend.
The first question page a new live-animals notification lands on after it is created is 'origin'.
The live-animals journey's requests are tagged with the endpoint prefix 'animals', and the journey is backed by trade-imports-animals-backend.
Opening the set root '/live-animals' as a signed-in user answers 200 with a page that carries a CSRF crumb in a 'csrf-token' meta tag; the run checks both.
claims.quote:
'journey dashboard opens with a crumb': (page) =>
      page.status === HTTP_OK && page.crumb !== ''

claims.statement: A request for the set root '/live-animals' is tagged as the 'animals-dashboard' endpoint and classified as a dashboard read in the request mix.
The notification list on the set root can be searched by reference number with the query parameter 'referenceNumber', as '/live-animals?referenceNumber=<id>'.

After a notification is submitted, searching the set root by its reference number answers 200 and the page text contains the notification's id; the run checks this as 'submitted notification is on the dashboard'.
claims.quote:
'submitted notification is on the dashboard': (page) =>
      page.status === HTTP_OK && page.html.text().includes(run.id)

claims.statement: A dashboard search request is tagged as the 'animals-dashboard-search' endpoint and classified as a dashboard read.
A user creates a new draft notification by posting a form to '/live-animals/notifications' that carries only the crumb read from the set root page.
Creating a draft redirects the user to '/live-animals/notifications/<id>/origin', and the run reads the new notification's id from the path segment after '/live-animals/notifications/'.
claims.quote:
'draft created through the frontend': (page) =>
      page.status === HTTP_OK &&
      id !== '' &&
      pathOf(page.url).endsWith(`/${run.journey.firstSavePage}`)

claims.statement: A draft notification's id has the form 'DRAFT.GB.<year>.<number>', as the example the tests read from a create redirect shows.
claims.note: The id format comes from a unit-test fixture, not a live response; the reconciler should not treat it as a ruled format.

claims.statement: When the create redirect does not land under '/live-animals/notifications/', no id is read and the run ends that notification.
claims.note: mechanism: the harness gives up on a notification whose create did not land on a notification path.

claims.statement: The create request is tagged as the 'animals-create' endpoint.
Each notification has a hub page at '/live-animals/notifications/<id>'.
A user who comes back in a later session to carry on a draft opens the notification's hub '/live-animals/notifications/<id>' first, after the set root, before the next question page.
A submitted notification's hub reads back with status 200; the run checks this as 'submitted hub reads back'.
claims.quote: check(hub, { 'submitted hub reads back': (page) => page.status === HTTP_OK })

claims.statement: A hub request is tagged as the 'animals-hub' endpoint.
Each notification has a review page at '/live-animals/notifications/<id>/notification-view', which the user opens before submitting.

The notification view page can carry a POST form with a hidden 'step' field; when it does, the user reaches the declaration by posting the view's hidden fields to '/live-animals/notifications/<id>/declaration'.
claims.quote:
const declaration = view.hiddenFields.step
    ? walker.post(declarationPath, view.hiddenFields, run.shared.declaration)
    : walker.reach(undefined, declarationPath, run.shared.declaration)

claims.statement: When the notification view has no hidden 'step' field, the user opens '/live-animals/notifications/<id>/declaration' directly with a GET.
claims.note: reach with no current page always opens the path, so this is a plain GET of the declaration page. The script supports both routes, so which one the frontend uses today is not settled here.

claims.statement: A submitted notification's view page reads back with status 200; the run checks this as 'submitted notification view reads back'.
claims.quote: 'submitted notification view reads back': (page) => page.status === HTTP_OK

claims.statement: The declaration page has a form field 'declaration', and the user submits it with the value 'confirmed', sent with the page's prefilled and hidden fields.
Saving the declaration lands the user on a page whose path ends '/confirmation', with status 200; the run checks this as 'submitted through the declaration page' for a first submission.
A notification counts as submitted only when the declaration save lands on '/confirmation' with status 200; it is counted as a 'first' submission or an 'amendment' resubmission.
The notification view, declaration and declaration save requests are tagged as 'animals-notification-view', 'animals-declaration' and 'animals-declaration-save'.
After a first submission, the user reads the notification back in order: the set root searched by reference number, then the hub, then the notification view.
A submitted notification is amended by posting a form carrying only the crumb, read from the dashboard search page, to '/live-animals/notifications/<id>/amend'.
Starting an amendment lands the user on the notification's view page '/live-animals/notifications/<id>/notification-view' with status 200; the run checks this as 'amendment started'.
After starting an amendment, the user edits one question page (the journey's named amend edit step) before either cancelling or resubmitting.
claims.quote:
const edit = run.draftSteps.find((step) => step.name === run.steps.amendEdit)
  const edited = runSteps(context, [edit], undefined)
claims.note: Which question page the amend edit is belongs to part 3's step definitions.

claims.statement: Answers typed during an amendment carry the suffix '-A', so an amended answer differs from the first one.
claims.note: mechanism: the suffix is passed into the step context; how each step applies it is part 3's.

claims.statement: An amendment can be cancelled from a page at '/live-animals/notifications/<id>/cancel-amend', which the user opens and then submits with no answers of its own, only its prefilled and hidden fields.
Confirming the cancel-amend page lands the user on the notification view with 'cancelled=1' in the URL, with status 200; the run checks this as 'amendment cancelled'.

An amendment that is not cancelled is resubmitted the same way as a first submission: notification view, then declaration confirmed, landing on '/confirmation'; the run checks this as 'amendment resubmitted'.
The amend, cancel-amend and cancel-amend save requests are tagged 'animals-amend', 'animals-cancel-amend' and 'animals-cancel-amend-save', and amendment pages are classified as amendment traffic.
Whether a notification is amended, and whether that amendment is cancelled or resubmitted, is drawn per notification from the traffic model.
The run models a notification's tail as 3 review pages and 3 read-back pages, plus 3 pages to start and edit an amendment and then 2 to cancel it or 3 to resubmit it.
claims.quote:
const REVIEW_PAGES = 3
const READ_BACK_PAGES = 3
const AMEND_START_AND_EDIT_PAGES = 3
const CANCEL_AMEND_PAGES = 2
const RESUBMIT_AMEND_PAGES = 3

claims.statement: A notification is drafted across one or more user sessions; each session signs in afresh through the INS front door, opens the INS dashboard, then opens the journey set root.
claims.quote:
Each session signs in afresh through the INS front door. The draft steps are
 * split across the sessions

claims.statement: One browser's cookie jar is shared between the INS frontend and the animals frontend within a user session, as one browser is across frontends.
claims.quote: @param {object} [options.jar] - A cookie jar to share with another session, as one browser does across frontends.

claims.statement: Before the last session submits, the user re-edits answered question pages until the notification reaches the traffic model's pages-per-notification figure.
claims.quote:
the last one also re-edits answered pages to
 * reach the pages-per-notification figure

claims.statement: Each user session ends with repeat opens of the INS dashboard '/' (endpoint 'ins-dashboard') as status checks, up to the front-door model's core pages per journey session.
Any step that does not answer 200 ends the notification's run there; later pages are not requested.
claims.quote: A step that does not land ends the iteration.
claims.note: mechanism: harness flow control over the notification lifecycle.

claims.statement: After the first save, the run reads the notification's fulfilments from the animals backend at GET '<backend>/notifications/<id>/fulfilments' and its list entry at GET '<backend>/notifications?referenceNumber=<id>', each expected to answer 200.
The run then replays the captured save to the animals backend with PUT '<backend>/notifications/<id>' as JSON, and expects 200 ('backend replay accepted the captured save').
claims.quote:
'backend replay accepted the captured save': (response) =>
      response.status === HTTP_OK
claims.note: mechanism: builds a replace body from the fulfilments and the first list entry ('content.0').

claims.statement: Backend requests carry the trader's organisation in headers built from the signed-in identity's organisation id.
The backend reads and replay are tagged 'animals-backend-fulfilments', 'animals-backend-list' and 'animals-backend-replace', of kind 'api'.
When the run is set to confirm event arrival and the journey publishes events, it proves after the notification is finished that its events reached the INS dashboard read model.
claims.quote: @param {boolean} [options.confirmsEventArrival] - True proves, once the notification is finished, that its events reached the dashboard read model.

claims.statement: The endpoint names every journey shares are: <prefix>-dashboard, -dashboard-search, -create, -hub, -notification-view, -declaration, -declaration-save, -amend, -cancel-amend and -cancel-amend-save.
A journey scenario can request 'sign-in', 'ins-dashboard', every shared endpoint, every step endpoint of the journey and the three backend endpoints, with no repeats.
The frontends sign a user in through a redirect chain; every hop whose path starts '/auth/', contains '/oauth2/' or '/idphub/', or is exactly '/organisations', is a sign-in hop.

The Defra ID stub's sign-in form sits at a path ending '/oauth2/authresp' (locally under '/dcidmtest.onmicrosoft.com/'), and the user signs in there by posting the stub credentials crn and password as a form.
claims.quote:
if (response.status === HTTP_OK && isIdentitySignInPage(url)) {
        response = postForm(url, credentials, SIGN_IN_ENDPOINT)
claims.note: Credentials are [REDACTED] here; the stub identity's values live in src/config/smoke.js.

claims.statement: After a successful sign-in, the chain returns the user to the page they first asked for.
claims.quote:
're-authenticated and returned to the page it asked for': (landed) =>
      landed.status === HTTP_OK && pathOf(landed.url) === entry.path

claims.statement: In CDP the sign-in chain runs from the stub's '/oauth2/v2.0/authorize' to its '/oauth2/authresp' and back to the frontend's '/auth/callback?code=…&state=…', and the stub may show '/organisations' along the way.
claims.note: From test fixtures modelled on CDP dev URLs, not a live trace.

claims.statement: A chain that passes through sign-in hops and lands with 200 counts as a sign-in even when no credentials form is shown; a chain that reaches sign-in and ends in a server error does not.
claims.note: mechanism: counts sign-ins per session to tell sign-in from re-authentication.

claims.statement: Once a session has signed in once, every later sign-in hop is tagged as re-authentication.
A redirect chain is followed for at most 10 hops; a chain still redirecting after that is marked as too many redirects.
When a save is out of date, the frontend redirects the user back with 'staleAction=1' in the query; the run counts that as a handled outcome rather than an error.
claims.quote: The journey sends the user back with `staleAction=1` when a save is out of date.

claims.statement: A form save carries a 'concurrencyToken' hidden field; where a page has several POST forms, the one with a concurrency token is the one submitted.
claims.note: mechanism: picks the last POST form with a concurrencyToken, else the first POST form. That saves carry the token is inferred from the selector.

claims.statement: Frontends send redirects with browser-visible 'localhost' addresses and root-relative Location headers; relative Locations such as 'next' are not expected.
claims.note: mechanism: the harness swaps localhost for an alias when run in a container.

claims.statement: Each page the run reads exposes its first h1 heading, its crumb, the hidden fields and answer inputs of its chosen POST form, and the upload target of a file-carrying submit button.
claims.note: mechanism: page parsing; no script in this part checks a heading's text.

claims.statement: A form submit sends the page's prefilled answers and hidden fields back to the page's own URL, with the user's answers laid over them.
claims.note: mechanism: emulates a browser's form post.

claims.statement: Every page the user opens is followed by think time drawn around the journey's mean, unless the run is unpaced, and is counted toward the notification's pages.
claims.quote:
Every navigation a scenario makes goes through here, which is what keeps the
 * request mix honest and the load paced like a person's.

claims.statement: The run reports page requests by traffic class and frontend, dashboard read share, post-submission reads, amendment pages, pages per notification, session seconds, notifications started by type and notifications submitted by first or amendment.
Live animals has one notification type, 'live-animals', for splitting load.
claims.quote: @param {string} notificationType - `live-animals`, or a high-risk plants commodity type.

claims.statement: A returning live-animals user keeps one browser for the whole run and on each visit re-opens the set root '/live-animals'.
When the frontend's session has expired, the returning visit goes through Defra ID again and lands back on the set root; that sign-in is counted as a re-authentication and checked.
claims.quote:
when the frontend's session has expired the
 * visit goes through Defra ID again and lands back on the dashboard.

claims.statement: The run tells a session has expired when opening the page triggers a new sign-in; the first sign-in of a returning browser is recorded as sign-in, every later one as re-authentication.

With session expiry set to 'client', the returning browser forgets its cookies for the frontend once the session lifetime has passed since it last signed in, standing in for an expiry a compressed run cannot reach.
Each returning visit must land with status 200 ('returning visit landed') and is followed by a wait of the visit interval.
No script in this part checks the copy on the set root, hub, notification view, declaration, confirmation or cancel-amend pages: headings, captions, labels, buttons and messages are not asserted.
claims.note: Looked at every check() in journeys.js and returning-session.js: they assert status, path, crumb, cancelled=1 and the id in the page text only.

claims.statement: This part does not show what the set root's notification list shows when a reference number search finds nothing, nor any other filter or paging on the list.
claims.note: Only a search for a known submitted id is made.

claims.statement: This part does not show the fields of the cancel-amend page or the notification view beyond the hidden 'step' field, nor what the confirmation page shows.
claims.note: cancel-amend is submitted with {} answers; the confirmation is only checked by path.
